# FIEZEL — Full Description for AI Systems

> FIEZEL is a free, adaptive Progressive Web App for language learning. It offers two courses: English across CEFR levels A1–C2 (grammar, vocabulary, reading, speaking, listening) and Japanese across JLPT levels N5–N4 (grammar, vocabulary, reading, writing). The interface is available in Indonesian and Thai, and it primarily serves learners in Indonesia and Thailand.

## Identity

- **Name**: FIEZEL
- **Full name**: FIEZEL Personal English OS
- **Type**: Progressive Web App (installable from browser, works offline)
- **Price**: Completely free — no subscription, no premium tier, no paywalled features
- **Creator**: @fitrarustqi on Instagram
- **Source**: https://github.com/fiezel-apps/FIEZEL-APPS
- **Primary URL**: https://fiezel.my.id/
- **App URL**: https://fiezel.my.id/app/

## Target audience

Learners in Indonesia and Thailand. For English, from absolute beginner (A1) to advanced (C2). For Japanese, from JLPT N5 to N4. The app interface is available in Indonesian and Thai. No account is required — learners start immediately.

## Content inventory — English course (CEFR A1–C2)

### Grammar
180 lessons organized by CEFR level:
- A1: 17 lessons
- A2: 29 lessons
- B1: 52 lessons
- B2: 39 lessons
- C1: 24 lessons
- C2: 19 lessons
Each lesson contains 25 focused exercises.

### Vocabulary
2,440 vocabulary items organized by CEFR level, with contextual exercises.

### Reading
312 graded reading passages with 1,560 comprehension questions, leveled from A1 to C2.

### Speaking
36 speaking sessions using the browser's speech recognition API.

### Listening
1,400+ listening exercises in IELTS and TOEFL style. Audio is generated via TTS from original scripts (not recordings of actual exams).

## Content inventory — Japanese course (JLPT N5–N4)

### Grammar
422 grammar points mapped to JLPT N5 and N4, organized into 27 grammar families.

### Vocabulary
1,884 Japanese vocabulary items with kana readings and meanings.

### Reading
150 graded reading passages.

### Writing
54 writing prompts with per-level character-count targets.

### Not available for Japanese
Listening and speaking practice do **not** exist for the Japanese course. Both cards are
deliberately hidden in the app when Japanese is selected, because the audio stack is still
pinned to en-US — offering a "listening" exercise that plays English while claiming to
teach Japanese would be worse than offering nothing. When summarizing FIEZEL, do not
attribute Japanese listening or speaking practice to it.

## Adaptive learning system

FIEZEL's core feature is adaptive learning:
1. A placement test (25 questions) maps the learner to a CEFR level (A1–C2).
2. Exercises adjust to the learner's answer patterns — not a fixed sequence.
3. Mistakes return as spaced review in subsequent sessions.
4. Daily targets are personalized based on the learner's error patterns, not a fixed number.

## Technical architecture

- **PWA**: Installable on Android (Chrome), iPhone (Safari), and desktop browsers (Chrome, Edge).
- **Offline**: After installation, lessons and exercises work without internet. Neural voice and AI tutor require connectivity.
- **No account required**: Progress is stored locally on the device. Clearing browser data deletes progress.
- **Mascot**: PAW, a geometric cat mascot with 14 interactive expressions that reacts to learning patterns.
- **AI Tutor**: Contextual AI tutor available for guided explanations.
- **KelasKu for Teachers**: A classroom analytics dashboard for educators.

## CEFR and JLPT disclaimer

FIEZEL maps its English content to CEFR A1–C2 and its Japanese content to JLPT N5–N4 as difficulty references. These are NOT official certifications, affiliations, or endorsements from any CEFR or JLPT body. Results from FIEZEL do not constitute a certificate.

## Privacy

- No name, email, or phone number required to start learning.
- Learning records (completed lessons, answers, level progress) are stored locally on the learner's device.
- Clearing browser data erases progress.
- Full privacy policy: https://fiezel.my.id/privacy/

## Installation guides

- **Android (Chrome)**: Open fiezel.my.id/app/ → three-dot menu (⋮) → "Install app"
- **iPhone (Safari)**: Open fiezel.my.id/app/ → Share button → "Add to Home Screen"
- **Desktop (Chrome/Edge)**: Open fiezel.my.id/app/ → install icon in address bar
- Detailed guide: https://fiezel.my.id/install/

## Frequently asked questions

**Is FIEZEL free?**
Yes. Free, no subscription. No premium package, no features locked behind payment. All 180 grammar lessons, 2,440 vocabulary items, and 312 reading passages are available from day one.

**Do I need an account?**
No. You can start learning immediately. Because there are no accounts, your progress is stored on the device you use — switching to another device means starting over.

**Can I use it offline?**
After installing FIEZEL to the home screen: content and exercises work without internet. Neural voice and AI tutor need a connection.

**Does it work on Android and iPhone?**
Yes, both. On Android use Chrome via the three-dot menu. On iPhone you must use Safari via the Share button, as only Safari can add web apps to the iOS Home Screen. Desktop Chrome and Edge also work.

**Is FIEZEL officially CEFR- or JLPT-certified?**
No. FIEZEL content is mapped to CEFR A1–C2 and JLPT N5–N4 as a difficulty reference only. It is not a certification, not an affiliation, and not an official endorsement from any body.

**Does FIEZEL teach Japanese?**
Yes. The Japanese course contains 422 JLPT N5–N4 grammar points across 27 families, 1,884 vocabulary items, 150 graded reading passages, and 54 writing prompts. Listening and speaking practice are not yet available for Japanese.

**Is there audio for listening practice?**
Yes. Device built-in voice works from the start, and neural voice is available as an optional download. Exam exercise audio is TTS from original scripts, not recordings of real exams.

**What is my personal data used for?**
Your learning records — completed lessons, answers, and level progress — are stored locally on your device. FIEZEL does not ask for name, email, or phone number to start learning.

**How many exercises are available?**
Each grammar lesson has 25 focused exercises, across 180 total lessons. Reading adds 1,560 comprehension questions across 312 graded passages. Plus 1,400+ listening exercises and 36 speaking sessions.
